text.content:
Actor: Vorath, Demon Lord of Helheim (CR 15) — 250 HP, AC 20, spell save DC 20, +12 spell attacks, 2 Legendary Resistances, 2 legendary actions, one 5th-level slot. Tune for four to five level-11–13 PCs; at higher optimization add fiendish allies from your bestiary, not more HP.

Scene: the throne room from the Hellheim regional effects — Smoldering Air, Watchful Dread, Burning Whispers (all three are on his sheet's Regional Effects (Hellheim Throne Room) trait; tick Inside Lair? only if you want the +1 CR adjustment while he's enthroned). Put a "Lair" combatant at initiative 20 on the tracker.

The one big decision: his single 5th-level slot casts Cloudkill or Dominate Person — he cannot cast both. Everything below shows what each choice buys, so pick based on the party you're actually facing.

Goal: establish the fear engine before the party commits to melee.

  • Round 1 opener: Dark Burst (Recharge 5–6) — 20-ft radius, DC 20 DEX, 10d8 necrotic, half on save. It's his biggest hit and it's back 5–6 rounds later; always spend it on round 1.
  • Aura of Despair does the passive work: creatures within 15 ft start their turn on a DC 20 WIS save or are frightened — and frightened creatures take 3d6 psychic. Martials must choose: eat the aura to reach him, or fight at range and ignore him.
  • Dreadful Gaze is the targeted follow-up: one creature makes a DC 20 WIS save or is paralyzed until the end of its next turn — a fine thing to do to whoever the aura already frightened.
  • Legendary Resistance (×2): do not spend these here — a failed fear save from the aura is fine for him. Save both for a Dominate Person or a banishment/hold from the party. That's what they're for.
  • Lair actions: Gates of Dread stacks fear with the aura, or Hellfire Bolt to poke the back line at range.
  • Legendary actions (2/round): mostly the free-economy Shadow Teleportation to keep his 15-ft aura orbit moving, plus a second-attack Shadow Fork (+10, 4d8+4, half-heals him).

Goal: cash the 5th-level slot against whatever the party is worst at.

  • If they're melee-heavy or clustered: Cloudkill. 20-ft radius poison cloud, DC 20 CON, 5d8 poison on a failure each turn, and it moves 10 ft every round. Park it on the martials and drift it across the room. Concentration: DC 20 to break is steep, but if it drops, he still has the slot? No — spent is spent; pivot to lair actions.
  • If they have one obvious lynchpin (healer, controller, twilight-cleric): Dominate Person, DC 20 WIS. A dominated PC is a round of friendly fire and a moral problem. If the save succeeds, this is where Legendary Resistance #1 goes — Dominate is the single strongest thing he casts, make it stick.
  • While concentrating: he can still act — Shadow Fork, Necrotic Grasp (+12, 8d6, max-HP drain on a failed DC 20 CON), and the lair action keep pressure up.
  • Not concentrating (or the slot already spent): Eldritch Blast is his at-will pressure — +12 ranged spell attack, 1d10 force per beam; cast it at 5th level for two beams, directed at one target or split.
  • Misty Escape discipline: his reaction teleports him 30 ft and turns him invisible when hit. Use it to break melee without dropping concentration. Don't be shy — but remember it ends his aura threat for a round; alternate between escaping and tanking.
  • Animate Dead (3rd-level slot): cast it the first round he isn't concentrating on anything — the Zombie rises on his next turn and occupies a martial for several rounds (undead fortitude makes it annoyingly durable).

pages.name: Phase 3 — Desperation of a God (100 → 0 HP)

text.content:
Goal: spend everything; the demon lord does not retreat.

  • Legendary Resistance #2 goes to whatever threatens his life — a failed save against banishment, hold person, or a second Dominate bounce. Never let him be disabled; that's the party's real win condition.
  • Lair actions every round now: Ember Storm when they cluster (2d10 fire + catch-fire), Throne of Chains on the biggest damage dealer (restrained + 1d6/turn), Hellfire Bolt (6d10 if the target is frightened — stack it with Gates of Dread or the aura).
  • Dark Burst comes back on recharge — round 6–7, another 10d8 nova.
  • Dark Pact Healing pads the phase: 1d8+6 (1d8 plus his Charisma), usable six times per long rest — heal whenever he has taken a couple of hits and no legendary action is pending.
  • Horrifying Visage (2 legendary actions) when two or more PCs are within 30 ft — mass frighten feeds both Watchful Dread psychic damage and his Hellfire Bolt rider.
  • Death beat: Vorath doesn't flee — the throne rejects him. On the killing blow the braziers flare violet then die, the chains shatter, and his Regional Effects fade over 1d10 days. The one 5th-level slot he never spent? That's your hook: what was he saving it for?

Escalation valves: too easy → he starts the fight with the Zombie already animate and Dominate pre-picked; too hard → the Smoldering Air regional damage only ticks on turns the PC starts frightened, or skip the catch-fire rider on Ember Storm.

Slot economy (one 5th-level slot): Cloudkill = area denial for a melee party; Dominate Person = remove their lynchpin; Animate Dead (3rd) is separate — cast it the first free round. Dominate is worth a Legendary Resistance to make stick; nothing else is.

Legendary Resistances (2): save them for save-or-lose effects (Dominate bounce, banishment, hold). Never for fear or damage rider saves.

Lair action picker:

  • Hellfire Bolt — ranged pressure; +6d10 when the target is frightened.
  • Gates of Dread — AoE fear that feeds the aura and the bolt rider.
  • Ember Storm — cluster punisher; catch-fire rider taxes healer actions.
  • Throne of Chains — restrain the biggest damage threat.
  • Lair Shadow Step — grappled or cornered; reposition to the throne.

Fear engine math: Aura of Despair (15 ft, WIS 20) + Gates of Dread + Watchful Dread (1d6 psychic per frightened turn) + Hellfire Bolt 6d10 rider = frightened PCs take psychic every round and feed his biggest attacks. Break the engine by spreading out and burning the aura down.

Concentration watch: Cloudkill or Dominate is his only ongoing threat — DC 20 to break, but a frightened-and-restrained caster PC still tries. If it drops early, his next big action is always Dark Burst on the cluster that broke it.

The nobody-sees clock: Necrotic Grasp reduces hit point maximum; Shadow Fork half-heals him. Track both — a healed-up Vorath in round 5 with a drained party is the fight actually working as designed.
